correctness.summary: Equality in the published partition bound plus Cauchy equality fixes the quotient spectrum. A trace-of-squares argument forces the normalized adjacency matrix onto the color-indicator subspace; zero quotient diagonal then forces equal color-class volumes and the cross-edge formula w_uv=d_u d_v/((r-1)A). The converse spectrum is computed directly, including the r=n boundary case.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The motivating 2026 paper explicitly states its equality classification only for the unweighted case. Searches across weighted Kemeny, chromatic equality, weighted multipartite normalized spectra, rank-one bipartite weights, and degree-corrected block factorizations found no equivalent or stronger classification. Closely related inspected sources concern the unweighted bipartite case, unweighted multipartite normalized spectra, or general degree-corrected matrix factorizations rather than this equality problem.

value.summary: The theorem closes an explicit weighted equality gap and reveals that stationary-mass balance, rather than cardinality balance, is the correct rigidity condition. It parameterizes every equality weighting, shows every complete multipartite shape can attain equality after weighting, gives a rank-one bipartite criterion, and identifies the dimension of the equality cone.

limitations: Finite connected undirected graphs with strictly positive weights on present edges are assumed.
The Kemeny convention is the one used in arXiv:2609.17481.
Numerical verification is supporting evidence and does not replace the proof.
A differently phrased result in weighted spectral graph theory or reversible Markov chains, or very recent parallel work, remains a residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
